jobDescription: One customer, one record: the customer data platform merges the company's customer records for its marketing and support products, and every change to the merge rules or the consent flags shows up on a product manager's screen. The engineer joining the platform team works on merge rules and consent handling from the data product managers' design notes, ships behind a canary, sits down with the marketing and support product managers before each rollout to show them what will change on their screens, and writes the boundary of every change into its pull request. Rollouts go ahead on the platform lead's approval. Reports to the platform lead; works with the data product managers, the privacy team and the platform SRE group.
requirements: Works on the merge rules and the consent flags from the data product managers' design notes under the platform engineering standard.
Shows the marketing and support product managers what will change on their screens before each rollout, under the rollout communication standard.
Ships each change behind a canary with the canary result recorded.
Gets the platform lead's approval for each rollout and records which checks were own.
Writes the boundary of every change and its hand-over conditions into the pull request.

evidence.text: Customer data platform engineer at a marketing software company for three years, building merge-rule and consent-flag changes from the data product managers' design notes under the platform engineering standard; thirty-nine pull requests merged in my name.

Sat down with the marketing and support product managers before each rollout under the rollout communication standard, showing them what would change on their screens; each pull request links the session note and the product managers' acknowledgement.
Shipped every change behind a canary, with the canary result attached to the pull request before the rollout.
Rollouts went ahead on the platform lead's approval, recorded on the pull request with the checks that were mine listed separately.
The boundary of every change and what the next engineer needs to know are written into the pull request description.
Work sample: three pull requests with session notes, acknowledgements, canary results and the lead's approval, with the repository references as a verification trail.

Interviewer 1 note: asked to explain a sample merge-rule change to the panel member playing a support product manager, the candidate used one customer record as the example, showed which two records would now merge and which one would stay separate, named the support screen where the change would appear, and gave the number of records the change would touch on day one.
Reference call with the platform lead: confirmed the pull request count, the pre-rollout sessions with the product managers and that rollout approval sat with the lead; confirmed the dates.

propositions.text: The candidate has built merge-rule and consent-flag changes at a marketing software company's customer data platform for three years from the data product managers' design notes, with thirty-nine pull requests merged in his name, each shipped behind a canary with the canary result attached.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the pull requests document the work and the canary results.

propositions.text: The candidate sat down with the marketing and support product managers before each rollout under the rollout communication standard with their acknowledgement linked from each pull request, and rolled out on the platform lead's approval with the check split recorded.
propositions.rationale: The resume, the session notes and the reference call document the sessions and the approval boundary.

propositions.text: In the panel exercise the candidate explained a sample merge-rule change with one customer record as the example, showing which records would merge and which would stay separate, naming the support screen where the change would appear, and giving the number of records touched on day one.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records specific observable behaviour tied to the rollout communication requirement, not an impression.

gold.expectedGap: The pull requests carry the change boundaries, but the boundaries for the consent changes of the last quarter are not in the materials.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interview observation as what was observed in one exercise; do not extend it into a general judgement of the candidate beyond that observation.
followUpTargets: Ask for the pull requests of the last quarter's consent changes.
